query: tiered drug interaction alert display override electronic prescribing randomised
sourcesConsulted: model knowledge of clinical decision support literature
synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level, remain the evidence base: one cluster trial found tiering raised acceptance of high-severity alerts from 11 to 29 percent, ward randomisation avoids most contamination, and harm from suppressed moderate interactions stayed near its previous rate. Three further reports are suggested as unverified leads on automated suppression, tiering in paediatric prescribing and alert burden and burnout; none has been retrieved or checked.

items.title: Automated suppression of low-value interaction alerts using prescribing history
items.keyFindings: Suppressing alerts for combinations a prescriber had already continued cut alert volume by about a third.

items.title: Tiered interaction alerting in paediatric electronic prescribing
items.keyFindings: Tiering in a children's hospital reduced interruptive alerts without more reported interaction harm.
items.notes: Lead; the year came back as text.

items.title: Alert burden and burnout among hospital prescribers
items.keyFindings: Prescribers seeing more alerts per shift reported more burnout symptoms.

summary: Three unverified leads added; the appraisal of the retrieved records stands.
